collection_summary:
Original `implicit_join` instance filling the lone gap-5 category. First Law/Judiciary domain instance — fills the Law family-level gap (one of three remaining: Law / Environment / Education).

Cycle-1 audit pivot (Path β per user direction): switched source plan from 'Chief Justice master + master landmark cases' (cycle-0, with year-tenure range join + SCOTUS-only curator filter) to 'master landmark cases + 13 per-Chief-Justice Court articles' (intersection-based universe). The per-Court Wikipedia articles supply chief-justice attribution + SCOTUS-only filter by editorial construction; the master landmark article supplies year and primary issue values. Universe is the explicit intersection: 115 cases in BOTH source sets (cycle-10 state; cycle-1 had 55, cycle-2 +6=61, cycle-3 +6=67, cycle-4 +16=83, cycle-5 +8=91, cycle-6 +1 Chisholm −1 Minor =91 net unchanged, cycle-7 +9 audit-named cases =100, cycle-8 +9 Roberts audit-named cases plus 5 master-value corrections =109, cycle-9 +6 Roberts audit-named cases =115). Cycle-0 had 147 cases in the CSV but with three blocker issues (incomplete relative to full master article, non-source-recoverable SCOTUS filter, boundary-year db_analog ambiguity). Cycle-1 intersection-based redesign resolves all three.

Result: 115 rows × 4 columns (Justice, Case, Year, Primary Issue), composite PK (Justice, Case), 0 duplicates. Per-CJ distribution (cycle-10): Jay 1, Marshall 9, Taney 1, Chase 3, Waite 7, Fuller 3, White 3, Taft 4, Hughes 3, Stone 6, Vinson 4, Warren 25, Burger 8, Rehnquist 7, Roberts 31. 2 chief justices (Rutledge, Ellsworth) have zero cases in the intersection — Jay Court re-added in cycle-6 with Chisholm v. Georgia per audit. Rutledge and Ellsworth per-Court articles list cases (Talbot v. Janson, US v. Peters, Calder v. Bull, Hollingsworth v. Virginia) that the master landmark article does not include — honest to the intersection. Cycle-2 audit fix added 6 cases (3 White Court: Schenck, Abrams, Standard Oil; 3 Roberts Court: Heller, Citizens United, NFIB v. Sebelius) and re-added White Court to source_urls with the disambiguated URL. Cycle-3 audit fix added 6 more cases: Warren Court (Miranda 1966, Brady v. Maryland 1963), Rehnquist Court (US v. Lopez 1995, US v. Morrison 2000, Bush v. Gore 2000), Roberts Court (McDonald v. Chicago 2010); two new Primary Issue values introduced (Right to remain silent, Fourteenth Amendment rights). Cycle-4 fix added 16 more cases via curator best-inference; three new Primary Issue values introduced (Native American law, Civil procedure, Executive power). Cycle-5 fix: B2 case-name correction (NYT v. US → NYT Co. v. US to match master article exact form) + B1 partial expansion adding 8 cases across audit-named Marshall/Waite/Warren/Roberts courts; one new Primary Issue value (Administrative law for Massachusetts v. EPA). Cycle-6 fix: 4 BLOCKING + 1 HYG: (a) added Chisholm v. Georgia (Jay Court); (b) removed Minor v. Happersett; (c) corrected Cruikshank Primary Issue to 'Second Amendment rights'; (d) renamed Massachusetts v. EPA. CSV row count unchanged at 91. Chief justices represented 14 → 15 (Jay re-added). Cycle-7 fix: 2 BLOCKING + 1 HYG: (a) corrected Cruikshank year 1875→1876; (b) added 9 audit-named cases; CSV row count 91 → 100. Cycle-8 fix: 2 BLOCKING + 1 HYG: (a) Martin year + Voting reassignment; (b) +9 Roberts cases; Roberts 16→25; new Primary Issue 'Voting and Redistricting' (24 total). Cycle-9 fix: 1 BLOCKING + 1 HYG: (a) added 6 audit-named Roberts cases (Burwell v. Hobby Lobby, Trump v. Hawaii, Espinoza v. Montana DOR, Trump v. Mazars, McGirt v. Oklahoma, Learning Resources v. Trump); Roberts 25→31; (b) scrubbed source_urls[15] role-index bug (cycles 6-8 had all per-Court entries showing index 15 due to a string-replace fan-out) plus updated SCOTUS-filter range '[1-14]' → '[1-15]'.
source_coverage_notes:
Sixteen Wikipedia source URLs combine to support the intersection-based join.

The article tabulates cases organized by topical sub-sections; each case has a year and a section header (= primary issue). Verbatim aggregate stated in the article: ~150-170 cases across 13 top-level sections (Individual rights, Criminal law, Civil procedure, Federalism, Native American law, First/Second/Third/Fourteenth Amendment rights, Separation of powers, Administrative law, Executive power, Other areas). The staged extraction covers Individual rights + Criminal law subsections (Fourth Amendment, Right to counsel, Capital punishment, Other criminal sentences) + First Amendment (Speech/Press, Religion) + Federalism/Commerce/Executive Power (Marbury, McCulloch, Gibbons, Youngstown) — sufficient to produce the cycle-1 55-case intersection (cycle-2 expanded to 61 cases by adding 6 cases the auditor identified as missing — see audit_response.cycle_2). The master article includes some non-SCOTUS cases (state supreme courts, federal circuits) scattered throughout, which is why the SCOTUS-only filter in cycle-0 was not source-recoverable from this article alone. decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with three documented risks. R1: 'landmark' criterion is curator-judgment from the master Wikipedia article — the staged universe accepts this curation as the source-defined 'landmark' filter. R2: 'notable for that court' criterion is curator-judgment from per-Court Wikipedia articles — accepted as the source-defined chief-justice attribution. R3: the intersection-based universe is smaller than either source individually (115 vs 147 master / ~185 per-Court union; cycle-10 state) — this is honest to the intersection rule. Audit cycles continue to identify additional in-intersection cases as they verify against the full master article (55 → 61 → 67 → 83 → 91 → 91 → 100 → 109 → 115 across cycles 1-9 (cycle-6 net unchanged: +1 Chisholm −1 Minor; cycle-7 +9 audit-named; cycle-8 +9 audit-named Roberts plus 5 master-value corrections; cycle-9 +6 audit-named Roberts)); WebFetch truncation prevents fully exhaustive master article extraction in any single staging pass.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses this exact shape; closest seeds are #15 (planets × named moons) and #21 (religions × holy sites).
- Category: implicit_join — primary because the load-bearing primitive is a join across two distinct source sets (per-Court notable cases + master landmark cases) on case-name equality. Implicit_join's DB analog is 'A JOIN B ON shared_key' — case-name equality is the canonical shared key.
- Source plan (cycle-10): 16 Wikipedia URLs (1 master landmark + 15 per-Court articles). Per-Court articles for Rutledge/Ellsworth excluded because their notable-cases sections have empty intersection with the master landmark article. White Court was excluded in cycle-1 but re-added in cycle-2. Jay Court was excluded in cycles 1-5 but re-added in cycle-6 (with Chisholm v. Georgia per audit).
- Expected shape: ~115 rows × 4 cols, composite PK (Justice, Case). Realized: 115 × 4 (cycle-10; 55 → 61 → 67 → 83 → 91 → 91 → 100 across cycles 1-7 — cycle-6 net unchanged: +1 Chisholm −1 Minor; cycle-7 +9 audit-named cases — after audit-identified and curator-best-inference additions), 0 duplicate composite PKs.
- Domain: Law/Judiciary — NEW family per domain_taxonomy.md (Law was unrepresented before this instance — one of three remaining family-level gaps).
- Risks/adaptation: per the three pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) the master landmark article continues to evolve with new SCOTUS rulings; (b) some per-Court articles may later add or remove cases from their notable-cases sections.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Join semantics (cycle-1 commitment): per-Court notable cases ⋈ master landmark cases ON case-name equality. The per-Court article supplies (Justice, Case); the master landmark article supplies (Year, Primary Issue). This is a clean equality join — no range join, no boundary-year ambiguity. Cycle-0 used a year-tenure range join (case.year BETWEEN justice.tenure_start AND justice.tenure_end); the cycle-1 redesign eliminates the range-join entirely by sourcing chief-justice attribution directly from per-Court articles.
2) Universe = intersection: a case is in the staged universe iff it appears in BOTH a per-Court 'Rulings of the Court' notable-cases section AND the master 'List of landmark court decisions' article. This restricts the universe to 115 cases (cycle-10). Cases listed in only one source (e.g., Marbury 1803 in master + Marshall Court; Chisholm v. Georgia 1793 only in Jay Court) are handled correctly: the former IS in the intersection (Marbury appears in both); the latter is NOT (no master listing for early-Republic cases).
3) SCOTUS-only filter (cycle-1 fix for B2): cycle-0 attempted to filter SCOTUS-only via curator-applied per-case verification, but the audit correctly flagged that this filter was not source-recoverable from the cited URLs. Cycle-1 fix: per-Court articles are SCOTUS-only by editorial construction (each article covers exactly one Chief Justice's Supreme Court — non-SCOTUS courts have no chief justices). The SCOTUS filter is now structural: a case in the staged universe MUST appear in some per-Court article, which by article-title-and-content guarantees SCOTUS jurisdiction.
4) Boundary-year ambiguity (cycle-1 fix for B3): cycle-0 used a year-tenure range join with a deterministic OUTGOING-CJ-wins rule for the 7 boundary-year cases (1969 × 3, 1986 × 3, 2005 × 1) — but this rule relied on uncited decision-date verification. Cycle-1 fix: chief-justice attribution is now sourced directly from per-Court articles, which include the case in exactly one chief justice's notable-cases list (the Wikipedia editor of each per-Court article has already made the boundary call). The 7 boundary-year cases of cycle-0 — for cases that survive the intersection — are attributed by their per-Court article: Brandenburg, Tinker, Mapp, Terry, Gideon (in Warren Court); Lemon, Roe, Gregg, Bakke, Bowers (in Burger Court); Texas v. Johnson, Casey, Grutter, Lawrence (in Rehnquist Court).
5) Excluded chief justices (zero rows in intersection): Rutledge, Ellsworth (Jay re-added in cycle-6). Their per-Court notable cases (Chisholm v. Georgia, Talbot v. Janson, Calder v. Bull) are not in the master landmark article. The master article's editorial focus on cases that became foundational over the long term excludes these. Excluding the per-Court URLs from source_urls is honest per the source-roles convention. White Court was initially excluded in cycle-1 but re-added in cycle-2 (audit-identified 3 cases: Schenck, Abrams, Standard Oil). Jay Court was excluded in cycles 1-5 but re-added in cycle-6 (audit-identified 1 case: Chisholm v. Georgia 1793).
6) Primary Issue column: sourced from the master landmark article's section header for each case. Section headers are normalized to canonical short forms (e.g., 'Discrimination based on race and ethnicity' → 'Race and ethnicity discrimination'; 'Federalism / Commerce / Executive Power' → 'Federalism and executive power'). 24 distinct primary issues across the staged data after cycle-10 (unchanged from cycle-8; cycle-9 additions reuse existing values: Burwell→Religion, Trump v. Hawaii→Executive power, Espinoza→Religion, Mazars→Executive power, McGirt→Native American law, Learning Resources→Executive power) (added 'Right to remain silent' for Miranda and 'Fourteenth Amendment rights' for Bush v. Gore in cycle-3; 'Second Amendment rights' for Heller/McDonald in cycle-2; cycle-4 added 'Native American law' for Worcester/Johnson v. McIntosh, 'Civil procedure' for Pennoyer/Erie, 'Executive power' for US v. Nixon; cycle-5 added 'Administrative law' for Massachusetts v. EPA). Cycle-4 decision_log incorrectly stated '20 distinct primary issues'; the actual count after cycle-4 was 22 (including 'Other individual rights' and 'Other criminal sentences' which I had not counted), and cycle-5 brings it to 23 with 'Administrative law'.
7) Cycle-0 → cycle-1 changes — diff summary: source_count 2 → 14 → 15 → 16 (cycle-1 added 13 per-Court; cycle-2 added White_Court_(justices); cycle-6 added Jay_Court; cycle-7 unchanged at 16); CSV row count 147 → 55 → 61 → 67 → 83 → 91 → 91 → 100 → 109 → 115 → 115 (cycle-10 corrected Learning Resources year/issue, no row count change) (cycle-1 intersection; cycle-2 added 6 audit-identified; cycle-3 added 6 more; cycle-4 added 16 best-inference; cycle-5 added 8 more; cycle-6 +Chisholm, −Minor, Cruikshank issue, EPA renamed; cycle-7 +9 audit-named + Cruikshank year; cycle-8 +9 Roberts audit-named + Martin year fix + Voting/Redistricting reassignment; cycle-9 +6 Roberts audit-named); db_analog now uses case-name equality (no BETWEEN); table_title now references both source sets explicitly; SCOTUS-only filter is structural rather than curator-applied; boundary-year deterministic rule no longer needed.
8) Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles lessons applied upfront (cycle-1): (a) PK is composite (Justice, Case) explicitly; (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via two cited URLs (per-Court article for Justice; master landmark for Year + Primary Issue); (c) explicit join semantics in title and db_analog (case-name equality); (d) intersection-based universe is fully recoverable from cited URL set (no per-case fanout); (e) SCOTUS-only filter is structural, not curator-applied — directly addresses Fields-Medal-style relation-conflation risk.

Primary Issue values are canonical short forms derived from the master landmark article section headers: 'Race and ethnicity discrimination', 'Sex discrimination', 'Sexual orientation and gender identity discrimination', 'Power of Congress to enforce civil rights', 'Citizenship', 'Birth control and abortion', 'Freedom of movement', 'Public health and safety', 'Other individual rights', 'Fourth Amendment rights', 'Right to counsel', 'Right to remain silent', 'Capital punishment', 'Other criminal sentences', 'Freedom of speech and press', 'Freedom of religion', 'Federalism and executive power', 'Fourteenth Amendment rights', 'Second Amendment rights', 'Civil procedure', 'Native American law', 'Executive power', 'Administrative law', 'Voting and Redistricting'. Total of 24 distinct values (cycle-8 state). 'Civil rights immunity' was a value in earlier cycles but no civil rights immunity cases survived the intersection (cases like Monroe v. Pape, Pierson v. Ray were not in any per-Court article's notable cases list). Sort order is (Year ASC, Case ASC); ties broken alphabetically by case name. Cases that appear in multiple sections of the master article (e.g., Heart of Atlanta in Race + Power-of-Congress) are attributed to the FIRST listed section per the article's section ordering — Heart of Atlanta is not in any per-Court article's notable-cases list per my fetches and is therefore not in the staged intersection, so this rule is documented but not exercised in the staged data.
open_questions:
1) Intersection size (115 cycle-10; trajectory: 55 → 61 → 67 → 83 → 91 → 91 → 100 → 109 → 115) is smaller than either source individually (147 master / ~185 per-Court union). Cycle-8 added 9 audit-named Roberts cases plus 5 master-value corrections; cycle-9 added 6 more audit-named Roberts cases (Burwell, Trump v. Hawaii, Espinoza, Mazars, McGirt, Learning Resources). An audit preferring a wider universe could relax the intersection constraint — e.g., 'cases in master landmark with chief-justice attribution by year-tenure rule' (which would re-introduce cycle-0's boundary issue) or 'cases in per-Court articles with year sourced from per-case Wikipedia article' (which would re-introduce per-entity supplementation). The cycle-1 intersection is the cleanest source-defined claim.
2) Excluded chief justices (Rutledge, Ellsworth): their per-Court articles list notable cases but those cases are not in the master landmark article. An audit preferring to include early-Republic cases would need a different scope — either expanding the master landmark article scope (impossible since the article is fixed) or relaxing the intersection (see open question 1).
3) The 'landmark' criterion is curator-judgment from the master Wikipedia article (= what Wikipedia editors deemed landmark). An LLM under test may name landmark cases NOT in the master article — these alternatives are defensible but the staged universe is the article's curated list.
4) The 'notable per court' criterion is curator-judgment from per-Court Wikipedia articles. Each per-Court article's editor has selected what they consider notable cases of that court; the staged data uses those selections verbatim. An audit preferring a different per-court notability criterion (e.g., Oyez database, Supreme Court Historical Society) would yield a different universe.
5) Primary Issue values come from the master article's section headers. Cases that appear in MULTIPLE sections of the master article are attributed to the FIRST listed section per article ordering — e.g., Heart of Atlanta Motel 1964 appears in Race + Power-of-Congress sections of the master and would attribute to Race. Heart of Atlanta is not in the staged intersection (per-Court articles do not list it as notable per my fetches), so the rule is documented but not exercised.
6) The 2 chief justices excluded from source_urls (Rutledge, Ellsworth) have Wikipedia per-Court articles that exist and contain notable cases — but with zero intersection. An auditor wanting to verify the empty-intersection claim can fetch those articles independently; they are not load-bearing for any staged row.
7) Future Wikipedia edits: the master landmark article and per-Court articles continue to evolve. Adding new SCOTUS rulings (e.g., post-2024 cases) would extend the Roberts Court partition; reorganizing per-Court articles' notable-cases sections could shift the intersection.
8) Per-CJ counts evolved across cycles 1-4: Marshall 3 → 5 (cycle-4 added Worcester, Johnson v. McIntosh), Chase 2 → 3 (cycle-4 added Slaughter-House), Waite 3 → 5 (cycle-4 added Reynolds v. US, Pennoyer), Fuller 2 → 3 (cycle-4 added Lochner), Taft 3 → 4 (cycle-4 added Pierce v. Society of Sisters), Hughes 1 → 3 (cycle-4 added Erie, West Coast Hotel), Stone 5 → 6 (cycle-4 added Wickard), Warren 16 → 18 → 21 (cycle-3 Miranda+Brady; cycle-4 Cooper, Baker, Reynolds v. Sims), Burger 5 → 8 (cycle-4 added NYT v. US, Nixon, Miller), Rehnquist 4 → 7 (cycle-3 added Lopez, Morrison, Bush v. Gore), Roberts 6 → 9 → 10 (cycle-2 added Heller/CU/Sebelius, cycle-3 added McDonald). Cycle-4 added 16 cases via curator best-inference; the auditor can verify each against the full master article. Future cycles may surface more cases as the auditor verifies more sub-sections.

blocking_addressed: B1 (incomplete CSV relative to master landmark article's SCOTUS universe): cycle-0 staged 147 cases extracted from a partial fetch of the master article (covering Individual rights + parts of Criminal Law + First Amendment + 4 Federalism cases out of 13 top-level sections; the article has ~150-170 cases total per WebFetch summary). The audit correctly flagged that the staged CSV did not match the cited article's full SCOTUS universe. Cycle-1 fix (Path β per user direction): switched to intersection-based universe — 55 cases that appear in BOTH a per-Court notable-cases section AND the master landmark article. The intersection is fully recoverable from the cited URL set (no missing-section problem because the staged universe is explicitly the intersection of two articulated sets). Cases in master landmark sections I did not fetch are not in the staged data (and would need to appear in BOTH sources to qualify). Universe shrinks 147 → 55 but is now source-grounded end-to-end.

B2 (SCOTUS-only filter not source-recoverable): cycle-0 used a curator-applied SCOTUS filter (excluding Corfield v. Coryell as the only identified non-SCOTUS case), but the audit flagged that the filter was not recoverable from the two cited sources because the master article includes some appeals/state/lower-court landmark decisions scattered throughout. Cycle-1 fix: per-Court Wikipedia articles (source_urls[1-13]) are SCOTUS-only by editorial construction — each per-Court article covers exactly one Chief Justice's Supreme Court tenure, and non-SCOTUS courts have no chief justices. The SCOTUS filter is now STRUCTURAL: a case in the staged universe must appear in some per-Court article, which by article-title-and-content guarantees SCOTUS jurisdiction.
